review_scope: Complete 352-line pinned application card read in two nontruncated overlapping ranges. Atomic capability, limitation, validation and responsibility assertions; referenced reusable/outbound dependencies remain separate. No full candidate accounting, independent omission audit, runtime assurance, rights or adopted policy.

claims.statement: Application-card applicability is feature-gated, not an unconditional declaration for all versions.
For GHES the card covers generic secret detection only; cloud Autofix, regex generation and Code Quality assertions must not be inherited.
Cloud Autofix proposes fixes for CodeQL alerts on pull requests and the default branch; proposals are not accepted changes.
Generic secret detection targets unstructured secrets beyond deterministic patterns.
Cloud regex generation and Code Quality are distinct capabilities, not generic-secret equivalents.
Autofix is available for CodeQL analysis without a Copilot subscription.
Developers evaluate proposed fixes for suitability and preservation of intended behavior.
Generic findings enter a separate generic-alert list for maintainers/security-manager triage.
Generic secret detection does not require a Copilot subscription.
Regex generator returns up to three candidates from description and optional examples; outputs need dry-run validation.
Regex generation does not require a Copilot subscription.
Code Quality combines deterministic CodeQL quality queries with LLM analysis; the two are not interchangeable coverage.
Cloud Code Quality findings use pull-request bot comments and a default-branch AI dashboard as different reporting surfaces.
AI-generated coverage workflows are an optional capability, not proof CI was executed.
English is the primary supported language for these AI security features.
Autofix language support covers a subset of default/security-extended CodeQL queries; language support alone does not cover every alert.
Generated regex candidates include AI-produced descriptions; descriptions also require verification.
CodeQL quality queries analyze changed pull-request code and periodically the full default branch.
LLM quality analysis operates on recently changed files after default-branch pushes, not a guaranteed complete repository census.
Generic-secret alerts support credential triage; a finding is not credential remediation evidence.
Generated patterns should be dry-run tested before deployment.
Autofix uses internal Copilot APIs to generate both code and explanatory text.
Generic-secret detection uses models, not only deterministic credential regexes.
Regex descriptions/examples are processed through LLMs and Copilot API; input-data handling must be reviewed separately.
CodeQL quality queries do not use an LLM; LLM analysis and Autofix use separate modeled pathways.
Model identity, supported models, hosting and training-data information are delegated to linked sources; not fully resolved by this card.
Pinned Autofix data is stated not to train LLMs and governed by Advanced Security terms; this is feature-specific, not universal AI data clearance.
Autofix prompts include SARIF, source/sink/flow snippets, approximately first-ten file lines and query help; not necessarily the entire codebase.
Autofix model output is stored/displayed as a suggestion, not proof of implemented remediation.
Generic detection input is repository text plus a meta prompt; users do not interact directly with the model.
Multiple models may validate a generic finding; this is a capability statement, not an actual target validation receipt.
Generic detection verifies returned strings exist in input and labels its alerts separately; this does not establish credential validity.
Regex generation sends descriptions and optional examples to an LLM through Copilot API.
Regex candidates can be similar and miss intended instances; three candidates do not imply three independently effective patterns.
Explicit result selection copies expression/examples to the form for dry-run testing; selection is not deployment.
Cloud quality LLM analyzes recently changed files with context and displays findings; suggested changes remain optional.
Pull-request quality Autofix consumes CodeQL findings and context and posts a bot suggestion only if a fix can be generated.
Autofix is nondeterministic; identical input can yield varied or no viable suggestions.
Complex multifile flows and subtle logic can exceed model capability.
Large-context truncation can prevent attempted fixes; absent output is not a clean assessment.
Autofix does not cover every alert type or language.
Operational capacity and failed internal testing can suppress suggestions; no suggestion does not mean no vulnerability.
Non-English code/comments may have lower fix success due to English-centric training/evaluation.
Suggested fixes can contain syntax errors.
Suggested fixes can target incorrect locations and introduce syntax errors.
Syntactically valid suggestions can alter program semantics and cannot infer author intent.
Suggestions may leave vulnerabilities unresolved or introduce new vulnerabilities.
Fixes may only partially remediate security or preserve functionality.
Dependency suggestions can be insecure, unsupported or fabricated; verify dependency changes before merge.
AI secret detection can miss credentials; users retain responsibility for code security.
AI secret detection may skip test-like paths and listed language extensions under stated conditions; these are coverage gaps, not N/A evidence.
Regex coverage depends on description clarity and may omit intended tokens.
Generated regexes may be invalid or inappropriate.
Regex generator targets structured predictable formats, not free-form matching.
Non-English prompts may lower regex generation performance.
Similar returned regexes reduce effective diversity of candidate patterns.
Code Quality inherits model limitations including incomplete detection, false positives, suggestion accuracy and bias; linked agent guidance remains independent.
Quality Autofix is best effort, not guaranteed for each finding.
Quality Autofix suggestions must be reviewed and edited as necessary before acceptance.
Evaluation uses independent runs to address nondeterminism and reports resolution, token efficiency, latency and tool reliability; no local target certificate follows.
Pinned evaluation policy excludes real user queries/customer code without permission; not a blanket data processing authorization.
Models undergo staged comparison against baselines across key metrics before release.
Risk/safety and evaluation-data details depend on separate reusable fragments that require review.
The described Autofix harness includes over 2300 covered public-repository alerts; benchmark scope is not target-wide security assurance.
Harness checks fixed alerts, new alerts, syntax errors and test-output changes separately.
Spot-checking and manual triage supplement harness success; passing CI alone is insufficient fix correctness.
Red teaming/filtering and continuing generic-secret efficacy monitoring are mitigations, not absence-of-risk proofs.
Regex dry-run validation is a preproduction safeguard, not exhaustive pattern effectiveness evidence.
Quality LLM and Autofix reuse other evaluation frameworks; shared infrastructure does not prove every target finding.
Autofix requires explicit human review/acceptance and verification of intended behavior.
Content filtering and internal testing can withhold suggestions; neither makes absent results a passing assessment.
Autofix is allowed by default for CodeQL repositories but can be disabled at enterprise, organization and repository scopes.
No-training statement applies to Autofix and retains governing terms.
False-positive alert volume feeds generic-secret improvement without access to secret literals; the card does not authorize exposing credentials elsewhere.
Generated regexes require dry run, explicit import and manual save/enable; generator does not deploy automatically.
Code Quality supports thumbs-up/down feedback; feedback is not binding policy adoption.
Consequential-use and legal/regulatory assessment guidance are separate reusable dependencies.
Review suggested fixes for actual vulnerability remediation and intended behavior.
After committing a fix, verify CI passes and the alert resolves before merge.
Verify dependency security/support and behavior, using dependency-review tooling where appropriate.
Verify each suspected false-positive generic alert before closing it with that reason; do not blanket-dismiss AI findings.
Dry-run generated patterns against representative repositories before organization-wide deployment.
Use specific descriptions and diverse example strings to improve generated regex quality.
Review every generated regex and description, modify as needed, and retain responsibility for adopted patterns.
Verify quality findings and Autofix applicability before accepting changes.
Provide quality-feedback signals to improve suggestions; this is advisory, not enforcement.
Human oversight must check AI output against expectations because it can be inaccurate, incomplete, biased or irrelevant.
Overreliance and sensitive-domain agent caution are delegated to separate reusable guidance.
Establish pull-request CI before enabling Autofix to check functional behavior after fixes.
Use pull-request dependency review to detect risky Autofix dependency changes.
Review organization Autofix suggestion metrics with an explicit time window; suggestion counts are not verified fix counts.
Evaluate generic-secret false-positive volume and establish alert triage processes.
Monitor Code Quality suggestion volume/quality and adjust enablement for organizational needs.
